cell.label: Sodium >145 mEq/L and serum Osmolality >290 mOsm/kg
Check volume status and order urine osmolality, urine sodium, and serum glucose
Hypertonic sodium gain, causes include, hypertonic IV fluids, salt ingestion, and primary hyperaldosteronism
Treat underlying cause, give diuretics, and free water repletion
Pure water loss: check urine osmolality
Replace free water; oral route preferred; IV solution of choice is 5% dextrose in water
Extrarenal water loss: hypodipsia and/or insensible losses
Hypotonic fluid loss: check urine osmolality and urine sodium. Urine osmolality <700 mOsm/kg Urine sodium >20 mEq/L
Renal hypotonic losses: diuretics (osmotic) or postobstructive diuresis
Replace free water; isotonic fluids if hypotensive; otherwise use hypotonic fluids (0.45% saline)
Extrarenal hypotonic loss: skin or gastrointestinal (lactulose)
